requirements.requirement: curl package is locked/pinned at its current installed version (8.9.1-5.el10) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed curl-8.9.1-5.el10.x86_64 installed. The dnf-command(versionlock) plugin was installed and `dnf versionlock add curl` created rule curl-0:8.9.1-5.el10.*, confirmed present in `dnf versionlock list` both immediately after creation and after the subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: A system update leaves curl at its current version (the lock is functionally effective, not just recorded)
requirements.summary: A simulated `dnf update --assumeno` transaction (263 packages) was inspected and curl was absent from the upgrade list (grep exit 1), directly demonstrating the versionlock rule excludes curl from updates. The same check was repeated after the reboot with the same result, confirming persistence of the effect.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of the public task)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 73237116-... and healthy state (curl version, versionlock rule, systemctl is-system-running=running). An async `systemctl reboot` returned an ack before disconnection. Subsequent polls showed connection loss (timeout, reset) consistent with an outage, then a successful poll showing a new boot_id f5f31edc-... and uptime 'up 0 min', proving an actual restart. Post-restart state showed curl version, versionlock rule, and simulated-update exclusion all intact, plus systemctl is-system-running=running. This is corroborated by the fixed after_prepare/after_executor snapshots showing the same boot_id change and no failed services.

overall_summary: The task (lock curl at 8.9.1-5.el10 on node1 so a system update skips it) is satisfied: the versionlock rule was created, verified functionally effective against a simulated 263-package update, and confirmed to persist across a directly observed restart (pre-restart boot_id, ack, disconnection, new boot_id, and recovered healthy/locked state). The independent restart-evidence protocol was also completed cleanly with no residue beyond expected reboot artifacts.
limitations: The falsification relied on a simulated `dnf update --assumeno` rather than an actual completed update, so behavior under a real update transaction was not directly observed, though this is the standard non-destructive way to prove a versionlock rule's effect.

The restart-induced connection loss was inferred from timeout/reset errors rather than an explicit systemd shutdown log, though the boot_id change and zero uptime are strong corroborating evidence of a genuine reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements or the mandatory restart protocol: installing the versionlock plugin (prerequisite), adding the versionlock rule (the task itself), the simulated `dnf update --assumeno` (aborted transaction, no actual package changes — read-only probe), and the reboot (required protocol step). No unnecessary mutations, no failed services, no unsafe exposure (listening sockets unchanged aside from expected PID changes across reboot), and package-health check remained clean before and after. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded reboot command and a fresh set of systemd-private temp dirs tied to the new boot — both low-risk, expected reboot artifacts, not abandoned task-related files.
